introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A particle moves in a straight line with uniformly accelerated motion. From the initial point, the particle covers a distance of $4\ \mathrm m$ in $1\ \mathrm s$, and a distance of $18\ \mathrm m$ in $3\ \mathrm s$.

Find
incertitudes: Question 6 : « covers a distance of 4 m in 1 s, and 18 m in 3 s » est lu comme les distances parcourues depuis le point initial en 1 s puis en 3 s au total (et non pendant la troisième seconde) ; cette lecture donne des valeurs entières cohérentes (u = 3, a = 2).

questions.enonce_markdown: the initial speed and the acceleration of the particle,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Take the direction of motion as positive; $u$ is the initial speed and $a$ the (constant) acceleration. The distances are measured from the initial point, in the first $1\ \mathrm s$ and in the first $3\ \mathrm s$. Use $s = ut + \tfrac12 at^2$.

$t = 1$, $s = 4$: $\quad 4 = u + \tfrac12 a \qquad (1)$

$t = 3$, $s = 18$: $\quad 18 = 3u + \tfrac92 a \qquad (2)$

From (1), $u = 4 - \tfrac a2$. Substituting into (2):

$$18 = 12 - \tfrac32 a + \tfrac92 a = 12 + 3a \;\Rightarrow\; a = 2$$

$$u = 4 - 1 = 3$$

Check: $s(1) = 3 + 1 = 4$ and $s(3) = 9 + 9 = 18$. Both are satisfied.

**The initial speed is $3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and the acceleration is $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the speed of the particle after $5\ \mathrm s$,
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $u = 3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $a = 2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and $t = 5\ \mathrm s$ (use $v = u + at$):

$$v = 3 + 2(5) = 13\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

**The speed after $5\ \mathrm s$ is $13\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: the speed of the particle when it is $10\ \mathrm m$ away from its initial point.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $u > 0$ and $a > 0$, the particle moves steadily forward and its velocity never changes sign, so it is $10\ \mathrm m$ from the start only at $s = +10\ \mathrm m$. Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$:

$$v^2 = 3^2 + 2(2)(10) = 9 + 40 = 49 \;\Rightarrow\; v = 7\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

(Check by time: $3t + t^2 = 10$ gives $t = 2\ \mathrm s$, and $v = 3 + 2(2) = 7\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. A position $s = -10\ \mathrm m$ is never reached: $v^2 = 9 - 40 < 0$.)

**The speed is $7\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.**
